subject: Post-call: Reranking model fit & validation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed rerank validation plan

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side focused on the reranking work we discussed:

1) Problem summary
- Goal: Replace heuristic score-based reordering with a learned reranker to improve relevance in your search results for product pages (goal metrics: lift in NDCG@10 and MRR without regressing latency/CTR).

2) Recommended approach (short)
- Two-stage pipeline: dense retriever (existing) -> candidate set (top 100) -> learned reranker.
- Model candidates to evaluate: rw-rerank-efficient (distilled cross-encoder) and rw-rerank-large (cross-encoder tuned for ranking).
- Offline eval metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, Recall@100; track latency p95 for reranker.

3) Initial offline numbers (example baseline vs. candidate — we'll populate and share full CSV):
- Baseline (current heuristic): NDCG@10 = 0.32, MRR = 0.28
- rw-rerank-efficient (prototype): NDCG@10 = 0.43, MRR = 0.38
- rw-rerank-large: NDCG@10 = 0.45, MRR = 0.41

4) A/B / rollout plan
- Start with offline validation and a small canary: 5% traffic -> 30% -> 100% if metrics look good.
- Primary online metrics to monitor: NDCG@10 (offline), online CTR lift, query latency p95, user engagement signals.
- Fallback: auto-failover to heuristic if latency or online quality regressions exceed thresholds.

5) Deliverables we will provide this week
- Benchmark CSV with NDCG/MRR by query bucket (attached).
- Prompt set / evaluation queries and judge instructions (attached).
- Slides with proposed A/B plan and rollback thresholds (attached).

Next steps: I can send the artifacts now — Neha will follow with the specific benchmark CSV and Vivek will propose the validation monitoring checks. Can we schedule a short sync to review the offline numbers and the canary thresholds next week? I put a placeholder for Mon, Mar 8 in the calendar — open to other times.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: acme_rerank_benchmarks_NDCG_MRR.csv; prompt_set_acme_v1.json; rerank_eval_plan_slides.pdf

- On latency: what are we seeing for p95 inference for rw-rerank-large vs rw-rerank-efficient? We need to understand tradeoffs for interactive search.

I'll block time for Mar 8 but happy to move if Neha/Vivek suggest another slot.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed rerank validation plan

Alex — quick answers and attached artifacts.

1) Test split / labels
- We used a temporal split for offline (train cut before 2025-11-01, eval on 2025-11-01 -> 2025-12-31) to better reflect distribution shift.
- Labels: combined implicit signal (click > dwell > conversion) + small curated human-judged set (~2k queries) for quality calibration.

2) Latency (single-request, isolated inference on our rw-standard-a100 setup)
- rw-rerank-efficient: ~45ms p95 per candidate (cross-encoder on distill-sized model); end-to-end rerank on top-100 candidates parallelized -> ~120ms p95 total (includes I/O).
- rw-rerank-large: ~120ms p95 per request for the reranker alone in this config; with candidate generation it edges toward ~240ms p95 — so tradeoff is clear.

3) Attached artifacts
- acme_rerank_benchmarks_NDCG_MRR.csv (full per-query bucket numbers + confidence intervals)
- prompt_set_acme_v1.json (evaluation queries + judge instructions)
- rerank_eval_plan_slides.pdf (A/B thresholds, rollback conditions, monitoring hooks)

Notes: the offline lift I pasted in the recap is from a preliminary run — see CSV for per-bucket breakdown. We recommend starting with rw-rerank-efficient for the canary to minimize latency risk, then evaluate rw-rerank-large on higher-value query slices where latency tolerance is higher.

Happy to walk through the CSV in the sync.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed rerank validation plan

Alex — adding the validation / monitoring checklist from an SRE/CE perspective. Apologies for the long-ish list but better to be explicit: 

Offline validation (before any online canary)
- Compute NDCG@10 and MRR on holdout (per-query and aggregate). Provide bootstrap confidence intervals and per-bucket deltas vs baseline.
- Check for distributional shifts by query type (navigational, discovery, long-tail).
- Run manual review on top 200 queries where models disagree most.

Canary / Online plan
- Start: 5% traffic for 48 hours -> evaluate. If no regressions, 30% for 72 hours -> evaluate.
- Primary online metrics: CTR relative lift (by query bucket), latency p95, errors & timeouts, downstream conversion signals.
- Regression thresholds we recommend: NDCG delta (offline) should be >= +0.08 for full rollout; online CTR regression > -1.5% is a hard stop; latency p95 increase > +80ms triggers auto-fallback.
- Monitoring: real-time dashboards + automated alert if any bucket exceeds thresholds. Include a canary rollback that flips traffic back to baseline in <5 minutes.

A/B considerations
- We'll instrument evaluation endpoints to compute per-query NDCG/MRR for sampled traffic and compare distributions in near-real-time.
- Consider a hybrid approach: rw-rerank-efficient for all queries, and rw-rerank-large only for high-value segments (top 10% by revenue or query importance) via routing rules.

I'll prepare the monitoring dashboards and a short runbook for the canary. If you want, I can demo the dashboard during the Mar 8 sync.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — very helpful. I reviewed the attached CSV and the numbers look promising, especially the per-bucket lifts on discovery queries. I'm comfortable proceeding with the proposed path:

- Start offline validation walkthrough on Tue, Mar 2 (Neha/Vivek to run through CSV + judge set).
- Canary: rw-rerank-efficient at 5% for 48h, monitor the dashboards Vivek prepares.
- If canary passes thresholds, expand to 30% and then consider hybrid rollout that uses rw-rerank-large for top-value segments.

Please send calendar invites for the Mar 2 walkthrough and the Mar 8 sync for canary decision. Looking forward to the demo of the monitoring runbook.

— Alex
